factors.name: Size (nodes and duplicate labels)
factors.summary: Number of duplicate tasks (0.99), Size (0.99) and Token split (0.96) load almost perfectly here, so the factor captures how large a net is in nodes and outgoing transition arcs, including repeated and silent transitions. The density-type measures (Density -0.53, Coefficient of network connectivity -0.48, Average connector degree -0.46) load moderately negatively, so in this dataset larger nets tend to be sparser.

factors.name: Density and connector degree
factors.summary: Average connector degree (0.89), Density (0.81), Coefficient of network connectivity (0.80) and Maximum connector degree (0.62) load positively, so the factor reflects how many arcs meet at nodes and connectors. Connector Heterogeneity loads negatively (-0.72), meaning densely connected nets in this sample tend to use mainly one connector type, and Separability (0.58) also loads positively, which is less obviously tied to density. Density, Coefficient of network connectivity and Average connector degree also load moderately on Factor 1 (about -0.46 to -0.53), but the gaps are large enough that no cross-loading is flagged.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for a factor analysis (Bartlett's test significant, overall KMO 0.75). Two varimax-rotated factors explain 72.7% of the variance, in line with the two eigenvalues above 1 (5.46 and 2.20). Factor 1 is a clear size dimension. Factor 2 is a density and connector-degree dimension; the size and density measures are moderately inversely related across the two factors. Connector Mismatch stays unassigned because its loadings are low (communality 0.12). Sequentiality and Control flow complexity were removed by the MSA filter, and Number of empty sequence flows was removed because it is constant.
caveats: Average connector degree and Number of duplicate tasks have communalities near 1 (possible Heywood case), so their loadings may be inflated and the solution may be unstable.
Connector Mismatch is not represented by either factor.
Sequentiality, Control flow complexity and Number of empty sequence flows were excluded, so the factors say nothing about them.
The strongly negative loading of Connector Heterogeneity and the positive loading of Separability on Factor 2 reflect co-variation in this sample of discovered nets and may not generalise.
The result depends on the 288 nets analysed, the varimax rotation and the choice of two factors.
